# Binance email fixtures

> ⚠️ **Every `.eml` file in this folder is SIMULATED.** They were generated by
> `tests/emails.py` and follow the *simulated* templates in
> `app/integrations/binance/templates.py`. They are **not** real Binance emails and the
> sender domain `binance.example` is a reserved, non-existent domain (RFC 2606).

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `payment_received_v1.eml` | text/plain, simulated template v1, valid DKIM/SPF/DMARC |
| `payment_received_v2.eml` | multipart/alternative (text + HTML), simulated template v2 |
| `payment_received_v2_html_only.eml` | HTML only, quoted-printable, thousands separator |
| `spoofed_display_name.eml` | Display name says Binance, address is NOT an allowed sender |
| `spoofed_dkim_fail.eml` | Allowed From address but DKIM/SPF/DMARC fail (spoofed) |
| `forged_auth_results.eml` | Gmail's top header says fail; a lower, forged header says pass |

## Adding a real Binance email

See the README section *"Cómo introducir un email Binance real como fixture"*. In short:
export the original message from Gmail (*Show original → Download original*), redact
personal data **without touching the structure, the From header or the field labels**,
save it here as `real_<type>_<yyyymm>.eml`, add a template with `simulated=False`, and add
a parser test for it.
